sources: The name 'Jodhpur' is derived from its founder, Rao Jodha, who established the city in 1459

events.description: Jodhpur founded by Rao Jodha, a Rajput chief of the Rathore clan, after conquering surrounding territory from the Delhi Sultanate.

entries.notes: The article states the region was part of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire until 1100 AD. This refers to the pre-founding region of Marwar, not Jodhpur city itself (founded 1459). Included as regional context for the Mandore/Marwar area.
sources: Marwar formed a part of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire and until 1100 AD was ruled by a powerful Pratihara King
Rao Jodha founded a kingdom that came to be known as Marwar
Jodhpur soon took over that role as capital

entries.notes: Marwar (Jodhpur) became a princely state under British suzerainty following the treaties of 1818. Inferred from standard regional history.
India's independence in 1947; Jodhpur/Marwar acceded to the Indian Union.
Marwari/Rajasthani dialects and Hindi were the dominant vernacular languages of the Marwar region. Hindi used as the closest referential match.
Jodhpur was founded by Rajput rulers; Hinduism was the dominant religion of the ruling class and population.
sources: Rajput chief of the Rathore clan

entries.notes: The city's location on the Delhi-Gujarat trade route and interaction with the Delhi Sultanate and Tughlaqs implies a Muslim merchant and administrative presence. Inferred from regional context.

sources: Jodhpur was founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha

entries.notes: Described as a main trade centre of the 16th century; inferred city status from regional context and trade importance.
